title: Maple Mustard Salmon Tray
seoTitle: Maple Mustard Salmon Tray | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Glazed salmon fillets with roasted Brussels sprouts and carrots
subtitle: Glazed salmon fillets with roasted Brussels sprouts and carrots
description: Salmon fillets bake with maple-mustard glaze alongside halved Brussels sprouts and carrot coins for a complete performance tray.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Maple Mustard Salmon Tray in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch salmon. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat oven and prep vegetables
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 400°F. Toss Brussels sprouts and carrots with 2 tbsp oil, salt, and pepper. Arrange cut-side down on two half-sheets.

steps.title: Mix maple mustard glaze
steps.instruction: Whisk maple syrup, both mustards, vinegar, garlic, and remaining oil until smooth and emulsified with no mustard clumps. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Season salmon
steps.instruction: Pat salmon dry, place skin-down among vegetables. Brush half the glaze over flesh side until evenly coated and glossy. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Bake until fully cooked
steps.instruction: Roast 14–18 minutes, brushing glaze again halfway, until salmon reads 125–130°F and sprouts are caramelized at cut edges. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.instruction: Rest 3 minutes. Salmon should flake with gentle pressure and stay moist pink at center, not chalky throughout. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

proTips: Real maple syrup matters—fake syrup burns and tastes one-note.
Add dried cranberries to glaze for holiday-adjacent flavor crews love.
Farro or wild rice pairs well with the sweet glaze.
leftovers: Flake salmon into a grain bowl with roasted veg.
Salmon salad with extra mustard dressing next day.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Omega-3 dinner that feels special. Glaze caramelizes beautifully without a grill.
mealPrepNotes: Halve Brussels sprouts through the stem so they stay intact. Mix glaze in squeeze bottle. Station: Place sprouts cut-side down for maximum caramelization on the flat cut surface. Station: Glaze salmon twice—mid-cook and final 3 minutes—for lacquered finish. Station: Hold at 150°F max—overholding dries salmon fast.
